decisions.executionNote: Raise and turn both open grippers downward, keeping separate left/right workspaces; establish safe overhead approach.
Retry with smaller continuous rotation and translation increments after zero-step IK rejection.
Complete downward wrist orientation and approach green pepper with left arm, red pepper with right arm from above.
Visually align downward grippers with green and red peppers and descend cautiously toward grasp height.
Close on the centered green and red peppers and lift slightly to verify retention visually.
Carry visibly retained peppers toward opposite sides of the middle basket, lifting above its rim without crossing arms.
Replan slower and slightly lower after continuity stop, carrying both peppers to the middle basket while maintaining elbow-up reach margin.
Tilt held peppers forward over the blue basket rather than extend the elbows further; bring green pepper to basket's left half.
Green pepper slipped onto the table; retreat left for a later regrasp. Slowly tilt and advance the retained red pepper over the blue rim.
Back the red pepper away from the blue front rim and raise it for clearance. Re-align the left open gripper over the slipped green pepper.
Use a small rotation bridge to respect the last accepted IK target, then retract and raise red while approaching green.
Regrasp green and lift vertically. Raise red substantially above the basket rim before advancing, maintaining forward wrist tilt.
Advance raised red over the middle basket; reopen and realign left gripper above the displaced green pepper.
Lower right EE to restore reach margin while tilting red farther forward over blue. Align left for a fresh green-pepper grasp.
Release red above the blue basket interior. Center and close on green, then lift and tilt it for rim clearance.
Red is visibly in blue. Green was missed: reopen and descend farther with vertical jaws. Move right back above the chocolate bars for staging.
Corrected rejected tensor: close and test-lift green; rotate open right jaws across the short axis of the bar.
Correct green grasp toward the near side and lower to its side-lying body. Lower rotated right jaws around the flat chocolate bar.
Close both jaws around green pepper and chocolate at their observed table-limited height, then lift vertically to check retention.
Both objects visibly retained. Lift and tilt green toward blue; carry chocolate to a central front staging point without crossing arms.
Release green inside the middle basket; set chocolate gently on the central-front table for a left-arm pickup.
Corrected zero-motion tensor. Approach yellow pepper with left and second chocolate with right using separated workspaces.
Descend around centered yellow pepper and second chocolate, then close without lateral motion.
Lift yellow and second chocolate, then carry yellow toward blue and chocolate toward a second central staging spot.
Place retained yellow into blue. Second chocolate was missed; return right arm to reapproach it.
All peppers are in blue. Approach staged chocolate from its left end, and reattempt the thin second bar with a lower, corrected right grasp.
Align left jaws across the staged bar's left end. Correct right grasp along and across the thin bar before closing.
Center and lower left jaws onto the staged chocolate's end; test-lift the thin chocolate with right.
Lift and carry the grasped chocolate toward white. Recenter the missed thin bar between right jaws and descend.
Left bar slipped: reapproach with a slight sideways tool tilt for a deeper central grip. Close centered right jaws on thin chocolate and test-lift.
Both bars remain on table. Lower open jaws farther with slow vertical alignment; correct right wrist to vertical before the thin-bar grasp.
At table-limited height, correct lateral jaw centering on both bars, close and perform a slow short test lift.
Lift the firmly centered left chocolate vertically. Change right approach to grasp the thin bar by its ends after repeated short-axis misses.
Carry retained chocolate over white with forward tilt and rim clearance. Descend right for an end-to-end grasp of the thin bar.
Release the retained bar over white, then approach the left wooden toy. Adjust right to grasp the thin bar at its ends away from the red rim.
First chocolate is visibly in white. Test-lift the right end-grasp; straighten and lower left jaws toward the wooden lion.
Corrected rejected tensor. Recenter on lion with left and approach the central toy with open right gripper, staying on respective sides.
Lower around centered lion and close left. Align right over central toy using slight inward tool tilt while keeping the arm on its own side.
Test-lift wooden lion with left; close right around central toy after a small inward alignment, then test retention vertically.
Both toys visibly retained. Bring left lion to a central-front staging point; lift and tilt right toy over the red basket.
Release wooden toy in red, then retreat right. Lower and tilt lion into the center staging area, opening left for a safe sequential pickup.
Withdraw open left arm clear of staged lion. Approach lion from the right with vertical, open jaws for pickup.
Descend centered right jaws around staged lion and close, keeping left safely clear.
Lift staged lion vertically, then carry it toward the red basket with forward wrist tilt and clearance.
Carry the retained lion over the red basket interior and release alongside the other wooden toy.
Both wooden toys are in red. Reapproach the sole remaining thin chocolate with a vertical wrist; prepare a precise short-axis grasp.
Rotate right jaws across the remaining bar's short dimension while descending to inspect alignment before closing.
Use wrist view to center the thin bar between open right jaws, correcting both longitudinal and lateral offsets at low height.
Fine-center the thin bar, close at the low grasp height, pause and make a short retention-check lift.
The thin bar was missed vertically. Reopen and use a shallow tilted grasp like the successful first-bar pickup, keeping tips centered.
Shift tilted right jaws farther along the bar to place its body between the pads, lower carefully and close.
Test the tilted thin-bar grasp with a slow vertical lift, keeping right gripper fully commanded closed.
Thin bar is still on the table. Reopen and shift the tilted approach along its length to bring the body deeper between the gripping pads.
Descend the offset tilted jaws to engage the thin wrapper lower, then close without sweeping across the bar.
Previous grasp missed beside the bar. Lift open jaws clear, then correct the tilted fingertip position toward the bar's center rather than the EE position.
Raise clear of contact and level the two jaw tips while retaining a shallow sideways approach to the thin bar.
Descend the leveled tilted jaws straight toward the thin bar, with a small lateral centering correction.
Wide open jaws appear blocked by the red rim. Narrow the pregrasp opening before descending around the thin bar.
Narrow jaws now descend without rim contact. Correct fingertip centering slightly, close on the bar and test-lift.
Thin bar still not retained. Use the narrower opening to reach lower than prior rim-blocked attempts, then close at the wrapper's body.
Change to a shallower side pinch of the thin bar, leveling the gripping pads and avoiding the basket rim with a narrow opening.
Lower the shallow side approach to the wrapper body with narrow jaws, then close without sweeping or contacting the red basket.
Repeated pinches miss the thin bar. Reposition vertically beside its right end to slide it away from the basket into a clearer pickup area.
Lower the closed, leveled right fingers beside the thin bar's right end for a controlled slide into open table space.
Slowly slide the closed right fingertips left along the thin bar at table height, checking whether it moves into clearer space.
The bar moved with the fingers. Continue a slow left-and-forward slide into clear central table space, with the left arm parked.
Slide the bar to the center-front handoff area without crossing the right arm; prepare open left jaws perpendicular to the bar's new orientation.
Bar is now clear of the baskets but rotated. Withdraw left, raise right and align open jaws across the bar's new short axis.
Raise and turn open right jaws to the perpendicular short-axis direction for the bar's rotated pose in clear table space.
Use the bar's current head-view position to align the fingertips, not just the wrist camera center, and descend with jaws across its short axis.
Make a small final alignment along the bar, close the unobstructed jaws, then test with a short vertical lift.
The thin bar appears between the pads. Lift vertically with the right gripper closed to verify a stable grasp before transfer.
Stable thin-bar grasp verified. Bring it to the central-front staging point and turn its length fore-aft for a clear left-arm pickup.
Set the retained thin bar gently on the central table, slightly left of center using tool tilt while the right arm remains on its own side.
Withdraw the open right arm to its side while approaching the centrally staged bar with open left jaws, maintaining separation.
Descend left jaws to the staged bar with a very small inward tool correction while keeping the EE on the left, then close.
Test-lift the thin bar with left, keeping it closed. Begin returning the empty right arm toward its home pose with continuous elbow-up motion.
Carry the retained final chocolate over white with forward tilt; smoothly finish returning the empty right arm to its original pose.
